summary: Specifies how Message Disposition Notifications (MDNs), such as read receipts, are handled in JMAP. It defines a data model building on the JMAP core and mail specifications, RFC 8620 and RFC 8621.

eli5.summary: A way for modern mail programs to ask for, send, and read receipts that say your message was opened.

questions: how to handle mdn in jmap
how to send a read receipt in jmap
subtitle: How a JMAP mail client sends and reads read receipts through two small methods, MDN/send and MDN/parse.

tldr.problem: JMAP clients synchronise mail with a server, but there was no defined way for them to send a read receipt (a Message Disposition Notification) or to look inside one they received.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9007 adds an MDN data type, a send method called MDN/send and a parse method called MDN/parse, announced by the capability urn:ietf:params:jmap:mdn.
tldr.outcome: Clients can answer a receipt request exactly once, using the $mdnsent keyword to avoid duplicates, and can display the details of a received receipt.

today: RFC 9007 is a Proposed Standard, published in March 2021, and its metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFC. It builds on RFC 8620 and RFC 8621.

sections.title: Why JMAP Needs an MDN Model
sections.content:
JMAP is a generic protocol for synchronising data such as mail, calendars or contacts between a client and a server. RFC 8621 adds a data model for mail on top of the core protocol in RFC 8620. A Message Disposition Notification (MDN), defined in RFC 8098, is what people know as a read receipt or acknowledgement.

The RFC lists three ways a client meets an MDN. When it receives a message, it may send an MDN to the sender: this document adds MDN/send. When it sends a message, it may ask for an MDN with a header field, which RFC 8098 already specifies and RFC 8621 can already handle. When it receives an MDN, it may want to show the details: this document adds MDN/parse. Matching a receipt to a sent message is already covered by the EmailSubmission object in RFC 8621.
sections.eli5: There are three moments: you opened a letter and want to tell the sender, you want to ask for a receipt when you send, and you got a receipt and want to read it. This document handles the first and the last.

sections.title: The mdn Capability
sections.content:
Support is announced in the JMAP Session resource with a new capability, urn:ietf:params:jmap:mdn. If it appears in an account's accountCapabilities, that account supports the MDN data type, parsing with MDN/parse and sending with MDN/send. A server that lists it there MUST also list it in capabilities, and in both places its value is an empty object.

Servers MUST support all properties of the new data types. Because keywords are case insensitive in IMAP but case sensitive in JMAP, the $mdnsent keyword MUST always be written in lowercase.
sections.eli5: Before using the feature, the mail program checks a list the server publishes to see whether it can do read receipts at all.

sections.title: The MDN and Disposition Objects
sections.content:
An MDN object carries: forEmailId (the received message it relates to; MUST NOT be null for MDN/send but MAY be null from MDN/parse), subject, textBody (the human-readable part), includeOriginalMessage (default false), reportingUA, disposition and finalRecipient. It also has fields the server sets: mdnGateway, originalRecipient, originalMessageId and error. extensionFields holds extension fields from RFC 8098.

A Disposition object has three string fields. actionMode is manual-action or automatic-action. sendingMode is mdn-sent-manually or mdn-sent-automatically. type is one of deleted, dispatched, displayed or processed.

These values are case insensitive in RFC 8098 but case sensitive here, and MDN/parse MUST convert them to lowercase. The RFC notes that a null reportingUA may have better privacy properties.
sections.eli5: The receipt is a small form: which email it is about, what the sender should be told, and whether it was opened by a person or automatically. The server fills in some boxes itself.

sections.title: Sending with MDN/send
sections.content:
MDN/send builds an email-style message from an MDN object. The request's using list MUST include both urn:ietf:params:jmap:mdn and urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail, the latter because of the implicit Email/set call and the use of Identity objects. Arguments are accountId, identityId, send (a map of creation ids to MDN objects) and onSuccessUpdateEmail. The response has accountId, sent and notSent.

The server generates originalRecipient and originalMessageId, and usually finalRecipient from the identity; a client-supplied finalRecipient is used only if allowed.

Duplicates are prevented by the $mdnsent keyword. The client MUST NOT issue MDN/send if the message already has it, and the server answers such an attempt with the new SetError mdnAlreadySent. The client is expected to set the keyword through onSuccessUpdateEmail, and the server MUST reject an MDN/send that would not result in $mdnsent being set.

Existing SetErrors are reused: notFound (no such email, or no valid Disposition-Notification-To header), forbidden, forbiddenFrom, overQuota, tooLarge, rateLimit and invalidProperties. An unknown accountId or identityId rejects the call with invalidArguments.
sections.eli5: To send a receipt, the program says 'tell the sender I opened this email' and then marks the email as 'receipt already sent', so it never sends a second one by mistake.

sections.title: Reading Receipts with MDN/parse
sections.content:
MDN/parse parses blobs as email-style messages into MDN objects. It suits blobs listed in the mdnBlobIds of an EmailSubmission object, or any message the client expects to be an MDN. It takes accountId and blobIds, and returns accountId, parsed (blob id to MDN), notParsable and notFound.

forEmailId can be null or missing when originalMessageId is missing, does not match an existing message, or the server cannot work out the match efficiently, for example when several messages share one Message-ID. The call can fail with requestTooLarge if too many ids are sent, or invalidArguments for an unknown account.
sections.eli5: When a receipt arrives, this tells the program to open it up and list who read what and how, or to say that the thing could not be found or read.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The RFC walks through three cases. In the first, a client sends MDN/send with a displayed disposition and an onSuccessUpdateEmail entry that sets keywords/$mdnsent to true. The server replies with the properties it filled in, finalRecipient and originalMessageId, plus an Email/set result. If the keyword was already present, the reply is a notSent entry of type mdnAlreadySent.

In the second, asking for a receipt when sending is done with Email/set create and a Disposition-Notification-To header field naming where the MDN should go, usually the sender. In the third, MDN/parse returns the parsed MDN for a blob id, or lists the id under notFound or notParsable.
sections.eli5: The examples show the exact notes passed back and forth: 'please send a receipt', 'done', and 'sorry, already sent one'.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered the urn:ietf:params:jmap:mdn capability in the JMAP Capabilities registry with intended use common and the IETF as change controller. It also registered the error code mdnAlreadySent in the JMAP Error Codes registry, with the description that the message already has the $mdnsent keyword and that the client MUST NOT try again to send an MDN for it.
sections.eli5: The new feature name and the new error name were written into the official public lists so nobody else uses them for something different.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The considerations for MDNs in RFC 8098 and RFC 3503 apply here too. The one new rule concerns identity: to reinforce trust between a user and the address they send as, the server SHOULD check against the provided Identity that the user may use the finalRecipient value, and return forbiddenFrom if not. The data model also points to RFC 8098 for the security considerations of including the original message in a receipt.
sections.eli5: The server checks that you are only sending receipts as yourself, not pretending to be someone else.
